articles.title: Briefly
articles.content: "Frankenstein" written by Mary Shelley, tells the story of Victor Frankenstein, a young scientist who becomes obsessed with the idea of creating life. He successfully animates a creature made from assembled body parts, but upon seeing his creation, he is horrified and abandons it. The creature, rejected by society and seeking companionship, experiences deep loneliness and despair. As it seeks revenge on Victor for its misery, a tragic series of events unfolds, leading to the deaths of Victor's loved ones. Ultimately, Victor pursues the creature in a quest for vengeance, but both are left to confront the consequences of their actions, culminating in a tragic ending that explores themes of ambition, isolation, and the quest for acceptance.

content.title: The Dangers of Knowledge
content.content: The pursuit of knowledge can lead to dangerous consequences, as seen through Victor Frankenstein's obsession with creating life, which ultimately results in tragedy.

content.title: Isolation and Alienation
content.content: Both Victor and the Creature experience profound isolation, highlighting the effects of alienation on the human psyche and the need for companionship.

content.title: The Nature of Humanity
content.content: The novel explores what it means to be human, questioning the boundaries between man and monster, and examining the moral implications of creation.

content.title: Revenge and Forgiveness
content.content: The destructive nature of revenge is a central theme, as the Creature seeks vengeance against Victor for his abandonment, leading to a cycle of violence and suffering.

content.title: The Role of Women
content.content: The limited roles of women in the novel reflect societal views of the time, emphasizing themes of motherhood, sacrifice, and the consequences of neglect.

content.title: The Sublime in Nature
content.content: Nature serves as a backdrop for the characters' emotional states, illustrating the sublime beauty and terror of the natural world and its impact on human experience.
